messages:
marie: Heads up — prepping the bundle + SLA carve-out playbook for exec review. Two asks we need to decide fast: per-route priority add-on pricing, and a contract soft-cap approach for pilot customers. Sharing options below.

sam: Paste the proposed numbers? Also what's blocking the launch criteria?

marie: Options: A) flat add-on $800/mo + per-token uplift (0.5c/token over baseline). B) tiered add-on (Small/Med/Large) with commit discounts (10/20/35%). Soft-cap choices: 100k tokens/mo pilot hard-cap vs named-account exception with pre-approved overages. Launch gates: legal signoff on carveouts, overage escalation playbook, telemetry in Console for per-route traces.

alex: Leaning B for flexibility. Also we should auto-fallback to lower-cost model when capacity constrained. For pilots allow fallback only to non-SLA models.

liz: Clarify priority lane: customers are asking for latency guarantees. We can't promise <50ms for all models/hard inputs.

daniel: Proposal: offer "priority lane" as best-effort latency SLO + financial credits if p95 exceeds target. Need to define credit math and caps.

marie: Draft credit formula: for each 10ms over p95 target -> 0.5% credit on that route's monthly bill, capped at 25% per billing cycle. This ties to Console metrics.

riley: That formula might be too granular for Legal. Simpler binary credit could be: if p95 > target by X for >Y hours, 10% credit. Much easier to explain.

sam: Legal will push back on complex tables. Let's prepare two contract templates: (1) detailed credit table, (2) simple binary remediation. We'll surface tradeoffs to sales.

legal: @sam + @marie noted. We'll review template language. Simpler option reduces ambiguity but may increase customer pushback.

ci-bot: deploy:contract-draft-v1 created - https://git.redwood/pm/bundle-sla/commit/ae3f4c :tada:

marie: Next steps: Alex + Liz iterate pricing numbers and priority-lane definition; Sam to shepherd contract templates through Legal; Daniel to run a finance model for worst-case (10 pilot customers breaching). Update due EOD Wed.

alex: I'll run the models today. Quick Q: do we allow per-route add-on stacking with Dedicated reserved capacity?

liz: No stacking — add-on applies per deployment mode. Exceptions require Sales+Legal approval and will be listed in contract annex.

sam: :thumbsup: tagging @legal for visibility and timeline sync.

marie: Also we need a short copy block for sales: 2 bullets on difference between priority lane (best-effort vs SLA) and dedicated lane (reserved capacity + firm SLA). I'll draft after the numbers are final.
